owner.label: Owner
owner.description: Has access to everything; can add anyone to the team and assign any rank.

admin.label: Admin
admin.description: Can change any server’s settings, edit economy data, make the bot leave and blacklist servers.

support.label: Support
support.description: Can see everything (servers, users, log) to help out, but can’t change anything.

co_owner.label: Co-owner
co_owner.description: Has access to everything and manages the team — but only ranks below their own.

developer.label: Developer
developer.description: Everything an admin can do, plus bot-level operations (e.g. re-syncing commands).

moderator.label: Moderator
moderator.description: Can issue and lift global sanctions and reload servers; can’t change settings.

home.description: The bot’s whole network in one place: servers, users, sanctions and a log of every change.
home.statusUnknown: The bot’s status is unknown (bot 6.1 required)
home.statusOnline: The bot is running · {shards} shards · last report {when}
home.statusOffline: The bot isn’t responding · last report {when}

bot.title: Bot status
bot.description: The bot reports every 30 seconds: shards, latency, memory, database. The page refreshes on its own.
bot.unreadableText: The `bot_status` table isn’t available — bot version 6.1 creates it, and the web database user needs SELECT on it.
bot.notReportedText: (Re)start the bot with version 6.1 — it appears here within half a minute.
bot.notResponding: The bot isn’t responding (or a shard isn’t ready)
bot.loopLagNote: the largest since the last report
bot.unavailableNote: a sign of a Discord outage if many
bot.failedExtensions: Failed to load: {list} — the reason is in the bot’s log.
bot.commandsUnreadable: The list of actions can’t be read (bot 6.1 creates the `dashboard_commands` table).
bot.noCommands: You haven’t sent any actions to the bot yet.

servers.title: Every server where the bot is (or was)

server.maintenanceText: If the bot isn’t behaving as configured on this server, have it reload the settings and permissions.
server.aiText: AI moderation, AI chat and the ticket AI assistant can only be allowed for a server here. AI triage (ticket priority) works everywhere without permission.

users.title: Find a user
users.description: By Discord ID (exact) or name (partial). The profile shows Discord data, economy profiles per server, sanctions and cases.
users.noResultsText: The bot only knows people who have already used it on some server.

user.sanctionsNote: Issue and lift in the bot with /global — when lifting, the bot also lets the member back in on every server.

sanctions.title: Network sanctions
sanctions.description: Bans, timeouts and flags that apply on every server of the bot. They can also be issued and lifted here (like /global in the bot) — the bot carries them out, and the result appears on the “Bot status” page.
sanctions.newText: Servers enforce it according to their own settings (Moderation → global enforcement).
sanctions.emptyAll: There haven’t been any global sanctions yet
sanctions.userIdHint: Right-click the user → Copy User ID
sanctions.durationHint: Discord allows timeouts of at most 28 days.
sanctions.reasonHint: The user receives it by DM, and it’s added to the servers’ moderation logs too.
sanctions.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Spreading scam links on several servers
sanctions.confirmText: The bot carries it out on EVERY server in the network. It can be lifted later, but until then the user is affected everywhere.

team.title: Who can manage the admin panel?
team.ownerText: You can add members, change their rank or remove them — always only those ranked below you. Every change is logged.
team.readText: Only the owner and the co-owner can change the team.
team.removeText: They immediately lose access to the admin panel.
team.addText: You need their Discord ID (on Discord: Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode, then right-click the member → Copy User ID). The new member needs to log in to the dashboard again once.

blacklist.title: Blacklist
blacklist.description: The bot won’t stay on these servers: if invited, it leaves immediately. Servers are added on the server’s page (Servers → the server → Dangerous actions).
blacklist.unreadable: The blacklist can’t be read — bot 6.1 creates the `guild_blacklist` table.

audit.title: Every change in the dashboard
audit.description: Server settings, permissions, shop, panel team, bot removals, balance changes — with the old and new values, for 90 days.

profile.title: Edit balance
profile.description: {guild} — the change takes effect immediately and is logged.

ops.blacklistText: The bot leaves the server, and if invited again it leaves again right away. Data is kept; the ban can be lifted at any time.
ops.reasonPlaceholder: Reason for the ban (only visible in the panel)
ops.blacklistConfirm: The bot leaves immediately and can’t stay there as long as the server is on the list.
ops.leaveText: The bot leaves the server. The data (settings, economy) stays in the database — if it’s invited back, everything is still there. To confirm, type the server’s name: {name}
ops.aiOn: Allowed: the server can turn on AI moderation, AI chat and the ticket AI assistant.
ops.aiOff: Not allowed: AI moderation, AI chat and the ticket AI assistant can’t be turned on (AI triage still works).

db.title: Database
db.description: The bot's whole database, made understandable: tables in groups, browsing, editing and an SQL console. Every change and query is logged.
db.ownerOnlyTitle: Only the owner can open this
db.ownerOnlyText: The database panel accesses the bot's data directly, so only the panel owner can use it.
db.sourceAdmin: A separate admin connection (DATABASE_ADMIN_URL) — the rest of the dashboard keeps using the main connection.
db.sourceMain: The dashboard's main connection. Whatever this user isn't allowed to do, the database refuses — for narrower or wider rights, set a DATABASE_ADMIN_URL secret.
db.grantsUnknown: The privileges can't be read with this user.
db.grantsHint: Security tip: the panel blocks schema changes anyway, so SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE are enough.
db.noPrimaryKey: This table has no primary key, so it's read-only here — use the console to change it.
db.revealHint: Sensitive data (e.g. a token) — click to show
db.changedFields: {count, plural, one {# field changed} other {# fields changed}}
db.consoleDescription: Reads run in read-only mode by default. To write, switch on Write mode: a dry run first shows how many rows it would touch, and only then do you commit.
db.committed: Done: {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} changed
db.writeModeHint: Write mode: INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE first runs as a dry run (rolled back) and is only committed after you confirm.
db.readModeHint: Read mode: read-only transaction, at most 1000 rows, 15 s time limit. It can't change anything.
db.previewTitle: This would affect {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}
db.unboundedWarning: Warning: there's no WHERE condition — it touches EVERY row of the table.
db.previewText: The dry run didn't change anything. Commit it?
db.historyEmpty: You haven't run a query in this browser yet.
db.readonlyText: Nothing can change in Read mode.
db.truncated: only the first {n} rows are shown — narrow the query

servers.description: Which servers the bot is on, their settings, the bot's status

dashboard.label: Dashboard and permissions
dashboard.description: The web panel team, its log, actions sent to the bot and command permissions

economy.label: Economy
economy.description: Balances, items, shop, jobs, fishing, underworld

casino.label: Casino and lottery
casino.description: Casino players, jackpots, lottery, casino championship

levels.label: Levels and quests
levels.description: XP, level rewards, daily quests, achievements

moderation.label: Moderation
moderation.description: Cases, warnings, filters, AI moderation, honeypot

global.label: Global sanctions
global.description: Bans and proposals that apply on every server of the bot

content.label: Messages and content

activity.label: Activity
activity.description: Daily message and voice statistics, invites

tables.guild_registry: Every server the bot is or was on: name, member count, active or not
tables.guild_config: Server settings (what you set on the dashboard): key–value pairs
tables.guild_blacklist: Blacklisted servers — the bot leaves them right away
tables.bot_status: The bot's live status per shard: latency, servers, members
tables.global_config: Settings that apply to the whole bot
tables.dashboard_admins: The admin panel team and their ranks
tables.dashboard_audit: The web dashboard log: who changed what, when
tables.dashboard_commands: Queue of actions sent from the web to the bot (e.g. posting a panel) and their results
tables.perm_roles: Command permissions per role (Roles and permissions page)
tables.user_profiles: Members' economy profile per server: cash, bank, chips, job
tables.user_levels: Members' XP and level per server
tables.duty_sessions: Who is on duty right now (open sessions)
tables.duty_totals: Duty time totals per member and type
tables.duty_log: The duty log: clock-ins and outs, adjustments, resets
tables.tickets: All tickets: open and closed, priority, rating
tables.mod_cases: Moderation cases: warning, timeout, kick, ban
tables.global_sanctions: Global sanctions across all of the bot's servers

blocked.multiple: Only one statement can run at a time — remove the others separated by semicolons.
blocked.ddl: The table structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE…) is managed by the bot's migrations — it can't be changed here so the bot doesn't break.
blocked.admin: Server, privilege and session statements (GRANT, SET, LOCK, CALL, FOR UPDATE…) can't run here.
blocked.file: Writing to and reading from files (INTO OUTFILE, LOAD_FILE) is not allowed.
blocked.transaction: The panel manages transactions: reads run in a read-only transaction, writes are committed after a dry run.
blocked.unknown: Unknown statement. Read: SELECT, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN — write: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, REPLACE.

rowError.nokey: The row can't be identified uniquely (no or non-unique primary key).
rowError.notfound: The row changed or was deleted in the meantime — refresh the page.

control.title: Bot control
control.description: Start, stop, update, live log and errors — without opening the hosting panel.
control.forbiddenText: Only the owner and developers can use the bot control panel.
control.tooFast: Too many actions in a row — wait a minute.

power.title: Server (Pterodactyl)
power.notConfiguredShort: The Pterodactyl connection is not configured.
power.setupIntro: The hosting panel (e.g. SRKHost) can start / stop the server even when the bot is down. Setup:
power.setupStep1: In the panel: Account → API Credentials → create a client key (ptlc_…). Leave the allowed IPs empty (the site calls from Cloudflare).
power.setupStep2: The server's short id from the panel URL: …/server/1a2b3c4d → 1a2b3c4d.
power.setupStep3: Give them to the site: PTERODACTYL_URL, PTERODACTYL_SERVER_ID (vars) and PTERODACTYL_API_KEY (as a secret), then redeploy.

invalid.url: PTERODACTYL_URL is not a valid https URL (e.g. https://game.srkhost.eu).
invalid.key: PTERODACTYL_API_KEY does not look like a client API key (ptlc_…).
invalid.adminKey: PTERODACTYL_API_KEY is an application (ptla_) key — a client key (ptlc_) is required, and safer.
invalid.serverId: PTERODACTYL_SERVER_ID is invalid (8 hex characters, e.g. 1a2b3c4d).

power.keyNote: The key stays on the server: the browser, the logs and error messages never see it.

errors.unauthorized: The panel rejected the key (401/403) — check PTERODACTYL_API_KEY and its allowed IPs.
errors.notFound: No such server for this key (404) — check PTERODACTYL_SERVER_ID.
errors.conflict: The panel cannot do this right now (e.g. the server is installing or suspended).
errors.rateLimited: The panel is rate limiting — try again in a minute.
errors.unreachable: The panel can’t be reached (network, DNS or TLS error) — check PTERODACTYL_URL and that the panel is reachable from outside.
errors.badResponse: The panel returned an unexpected response.
errors.rejected: The panel rejected the request (e.g. a limit was reached).
errors.timeout: The panel didn’t answer within 12 seconds — it may be overloaded, or the host’s firewall drops the website’s requests.
errors.redirect: The panel redirected — PTERODACTYL_URL is probably not the panel’s exact address (e.g. http instead of https, or a missing / extra www).
errors.blocked: A firewall in front of the panel (e.g. Cloudflare protection) blocks the website’s requests — API calls must be allowed at the host.

power.note: These buttons talk to the hosting panel — they work even when the bot is down. For a graceful restart (closing cogs and the database) prefer the Restart action below.

start.title: Start the server?
start.text: The host starts the bot process.

restart.title: Restart the server?
restart.text: The host stops and restarts the whole bot (every process in a cluster). It will not respond for 30–60 seconds.

stop.title: Stop the server?
stop.text: The bot goes offline until you start it again (here or in the panel).

kill.title: Kill the process?
kill.text: Immediate, NOT graceful — only if the bot is stuck and Stop does not help. Unfinished work may be lost.

sent.start: Start sent — the server will boot shortly.

version.title: Version and updates
version.noData: The bot has not reported yet (or bot_status is unreadable).
version.noGit: not running from a git clone
version.oldBot: The bot is older than 7.7 — it does not report git and process data yet.
version.mixed: Processes run different code: {list} — restart the whole bot.

actions.title: Bot actions
actions.description: The bot runs these within 5 seconds; results appear below. The bot must be running.
actions.offlineNote: The bot is not reporting — the action is queued and runs after start. If it is stopped, start it with the panel button above first.
actions.clusterNote: With several processes (cluster.py) restart, update and cog reload affect process 0 only; use the panel Restart button for the whole bot. Cache clearing runs in every process.
actions.queued: Queued — the bot will run it shortly.
actions.pending: This action is already queued or running.
actions.badCog: Unknown module — only modules reported by the bot can be reloaded.

bot_restart.title: Restart the bot?
bot_restart.text: Graceful shutdown (cogs and database closed), then the bot restarts with the same command. About 30 seconds offline.

bot_update.title: Update the bot from GitHub?
bot_update.text: git pull from the tracked branch (and package install if needed); if new code arrived, the bot restarts gracefully. Skipped if local changes conflict.

cache_clear.title: Clear the caches?
cache_clear.text: Settings, permissions and lists are reloaded from the database in every process. Safe; causes a short burst of queries.

cog_reload.label: Module:
cog_reload.none: the bot has not reported modules yet
cog_reload.title: Reload this module?
cog_reload.text: {name} is unloaded and loaded again from the code on disk. Its background tasks restart.

errors.title: Errors (24 hours)
errors.unavailable: The log is unreadable — the bot_log_lines table is created by bot 7.7.
errors.none: No errors in the last 24 hours.
errors.truncated: Only the latest 2000 error lines were grouped.

console.title: Live console
console.disabled: the bot does not log to the database (BOT_LOG_DB_LEVEL=OFF)
console.unavailable: The log is not available yet — bot 7.7 creates the bot_log_lines table.
console.error: Could not load the log — retrying…
console.pausedNote: Paused — new lines arrive when you resume.
console.liveNote: Live: refreshes every {seconds} s. Secrets (tokens, keys, passwords) never appear in the log.

hosting.ownerOnly: Only the panel owner can see the hosting files, backups and startup settings.
hosting.setupHint: Set up the Pterodactyl connection — guide:

files.name: Name
files.downloadReady: The download opens in a new tab.
files.secretRefused: This file may contain secrets (.env, key, certificate, credentials) — it cannot be downloaded from the site. Use the hosting panel if you need it.
files.truncated: Only the first {shown} entries are shown ({total} in this folder).
files.note: Uploading, editing and deleting are intentionally not available. Downloads use a short-lived signed link and are logged.

backups.title: Backups
backups.description: The host's backups. A new backup can be made any time (it changes nothing on the server); restoring and deleting are only possible in the hosting panel.
backups.noneAllowed: Your hosting plan does not allow backups.
backups.limitReached: The backup limit is reached — delete an old one in the hosting panel to make a new one.
backups.confirmText: The host saves the bot folder in the background. The bot keeps running; it can take a few minutes.
backups.created: Backup started — it will show as done in a few minutes.
backups.locked: locked (cannot be deleted in the panel)
backups.note: Backup downloads use a short-lived signed link and are logged. A backup may include the .env file — treat it as a secret.

startup.title: Startup settings
startup.note: Values of secret-looking variables (KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD …) never leave the server. Change them in the hosting panel.
